_meta.rule: Only these documents may be cited. A value that is not in a source on this register is left blank and appears on the Flagged for Review page. 'retrieved' records what this session actually opened and read, not merely linked.

sources.title_en: Regulations of the PRC on Foreign Exchange Administration (State Council Decree No. 532)
sources.title_zh: 中华人民共和国外汇管理条例（国务院令第532号）
supports: Art. 5: the State does not restrict current international payments and transfers
Art. 12: current-account FX transactions must have a real, lawful transaction basis
Art. 17: registration required for outbound direct investment / securities by domestic entities and individuals
Art. 22: capital-account FX payments need approval where required; a lawfully terminated FIE's foreign investor may purchase FX and remit after liquidation and tax
Art. 39: evasion of FX control - fine up to 30% of the amount, 30%-100% if serious
Art. 40: illegal arbitrage / fraudulent purchase of FX - fine up to 30%, 30%-100% if serious
Art. 42: illegal carriage of FX across the border - warning, fine up to 20% of the amount
Art. 45: private or disguised FX dealing - warning, confiscation of illegal gains, fine up to 30%, 30%-100% if serious
Art. 52: definition of 境内个人 (domestic individual) - PRC citizens and foreigners continuously resident in China for one year
sources.retrieval_note: Full text read on gov.cn; articles quoted verbatim above were checked in the page body.

sources.issuer: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), printed in the State Council Gazette
sources.title_en: Guidelines for Current-Account Foreign Exchange Business (2020 edition), Hui Fa [2020] No. 14
sources.title_zh: 经常项目外汇业务指引（2020年版）（汇发〔2020〕14号）
supports: Art. 49: service-trade payments above USD 50,000 need tax filing verification
Art. 54: individual settlement and domestic-individual FX purchase both carry an annual facilitation quota of USD 50,000 each
Art. 55: within the quota, ID alone is enough; counter or electronic channel
Art. 56: above the quota, a domestic individual may settle or purchase against ID plus source-of-funds / use-of-funds documents
Art. 57: the individual FX purchase application form and the individual's legal responsibility for it
Art. 58: a foreign individual settles FX against ID plus use documents; single settlements above USD 50,000 must be paid straight to the counterparty's PRC RMB account

Art. 59: a foreign individual purchasing FX against lawful current-account RMB income in China uses ID plus source documents including tax vouchers; a foreign permanent-residence ID holder uses the annual facilitation quota
Art. 61: close relatives may act for the individual within the quota, with authorisation and relationship evidence
Art. 62: splitting to evade the quota is prohibited; SAFE runs a watch list, with the listing lasting the current year plus two more
Art. 64: remitting FX already in an account - up to USD 50,000/day on ID alone, above that with supporting documents
Art. 66: individual cross-border e-commerce and market-purchase settlement does not consume the facilitation quota when transaction evidence is provided
Art. 67: transfers between accounts are limited to your own accounts and those of close relatives
Art. 86: cash withdrawal up to USD 10,000/day on ID
Art. 88: cash settlement rules, USD 10,000/day threshold
Art. 89: carrying cash out - USD 5,000 to USD 10,000 needs a bank-issued carriage permit; above USD 10,000 only a SAFE permit, and only for war-risk or similarly restricted destinations
sources.retrieval_note: Articles 54-67, 86-89 were read verbatim in the gazette text. This instrument is the operative current-account rule set and supersedes earlier inconsistent notices.

sources.title_en: PBOC Announcement [2004] No. 16 - Interim Measures for the Administration of the Sale and Payment of Foreign Exchange for the Transfer of Personal Property Abroad
sources.title_zh: 中国人民银行公告[2004]第16号 个人财产对外转移售付汇管理暂行办法
supports: Art. 2: personal property transfer abroad means emigration transfer (移民转移) or inheritance transfer (继承转移); an inheritance transfer is made by a foreign citizen or a Hong Kong/Macao resident who has lawfully inherited a PRC estate
Art. 3: the property must be the applicant's own lawful property and undisputed

Art. 6: the emigration transfer must be applied for once for the whole amount and paid out in stages - first no more than half, after one year no more than half of the remainder, after two years the rest; amounts up to RMB 200,000 may be paid in one go
Art. 6: an inheritance transfer is applied for once and may be paid in one or several instalments
Art. 8: documents for an emigration transfer, including cancelled PRC household registration and proof of settlement abroad, property title documents and a tax payment certificate
Art. 9: documents for an inheritance transfer, including proof of inheritance and the deceased's tax certificate
Art. 10: totals up to RMB 500,000 are approved by the local SAFE branch, above that by SAFE head office
Art. 11: the bank must remit directly to the applicant's own account abroad and may not hand out cash
Art. 12: applications are refused where a court or supervisory restriction applies, where the case is pending, where the property may not be transferred by law, or where lawful origin cannot be shown
Art. 13: false documents or repeat applications for the same property are punished under Art. 40 of the FX Regulations
sources.retrieval_note: Full text read on the SAFE portal. The page carries no repeal notice; no later instrument replacing it was retrieved this session, so its current status is treated as in force but is flagged for confirmation (F-04).

sources.title_en: Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (as amended 2018), official English translation
sources.title_zh: 中华人民共和国个人所得税法
supports: Art. 1: a resident individual (domiciled, or resident 183+ days in a tax year) is taxed on income from within China and overseas; a non-resident is taxed on China-source income

Art. 2: nine categories of taxable income - wages; personal service; author's remuneration; royalties; business operation; interest, dividends and bonuses; leasing of assets; transfer of assets; incidental income. Converting your own money is not one of them
Art. 3(3): a flat 20% rate applies to interest, dividends and bonuses, leasing of assets, transfer of assets and incidental income
Art. 4: exempt income list
sources.retrieval_note: English text read on the STA site; articles 1-4 quoted.

sources.title_en: Order [2025] No. 11 - Measures for Customer Due Diligence and Record Keeping of Financial Institutions, in force 1 January 2026
sources.title_zh: 中国人民银行 国家金融监督管理总局 中国证券监督管理委员会令〔2025〕第11号（金融机构客户尽职调查和客户身份资料及交易记录保存管理办法）
supports: Art. 34: on any outbound remittance the institution records and transmits the remitter's name, account and address and the payee's name and account; where the single amount is RMB 5,000 or USD 1,000 equivalent or more, it must verify the accuracy of the remitter information
Art. 35: an institution may not process a remittance that does not meet the Art. 34/35 information requirements
Art. 44: identity records and transaction records kept at least 10 years
Art. 52: in force 1 January 2026, repealing the 2007 and 2022 measures
sources.retrieval_note: Full text read on pbc.gov.cn; Art. 34, 35, 44 and 52 quoted. This is a 2026 change that most older guides do not mention: it is an AML verification threshold, not a quota and not a cap.

sources.title_en: Bank of China e-banking personal transfer and remittance tariff
sources.title_zh: 中国银行电子银行个人服务转账汇款费率表
supports: Cross-border telegraphic transfer: 1 per mille of the remitted amount, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260 per transaction
Cable charge: CNY 80 per transaction for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; CNY 150 per transaction elsewhere
Rates shown as effective 1 November 2014; local or negotiated prices may differ
sources.retrieval_note: Tariff table read. Provider-primary price, not law: a bank's own schedule binds only that bank and that product, and the page itself says local differences and negotiated prices may apply.

sources.title_en: Announcement adjusting part of the trade-finance service price list (effective 9 February 2018)
sources.title_zh: 关于调整部分贸易金融服务项目的公告(2018年2月9日起)
supports: Optional full-amount arrival (全额到账) on an ordinary telegraphic transfer: in addition to commission and cable charge, USD 15 per transaction where the receiving bank holds its account with BOC's New York branch, otherwise USD 25 per transaction
The charge is made because the overseas bank's fee is collected from the sender instead of being deducted from the principal
sources.retrieval_note: Announcement read. This is a corporate / trade-finance price list; applying its USD 15 line to a personal remittance is an assumption and is flagged (F-06).

sources.title_en: Guide to CNY transfers (Wise Help Centre)
supports: Sending from CNY is available to senders who are not mainland Chinese, or who have worked in China, with a China tax record showing tax paid in the last three years
Maximum single transfer from a China bank app: CNY 300,000
The overall limit depends on your declared China income and the tax you have paid
Money sent out of China this way can only go to another account you own
Personal accounts only; first-time verification takes 1-2 working days
sources.retrieval_note: Help page read. The page does not publish a fixed fee for the CNY-to-USD conversion; Wise quotes per transaction, so no fee figure is used here (F-08).

sources.title_en: 26 U.S.C. section 988 - Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions
supports: section 988(c)(1)(C): disposing of nonfunctional currency is a section 988 transaction

section 988(e)(2): on a personal transaction by an individual, no gain is recognized by reason of exchange-rate change after acquisition, but that exclusion does not apply if the gain would exceed USD 200
section 988(e)(3): personal transaction means a transaction by an individual other than one whose expenses meet section 162 or section 212
section 988(a)(1): foreign currency gain or loss is ordinary income or loss
sources.retrieval_note: Statutory text read. The USD 200 figure is a cliff, not an allowance: exceed it on a transaction and the whole gain is recognized. The page read is the 2018 edition; the provision wording has not changed.

sources.title_en: U.S. citizens and resident aliens abroad
supports: A U.S. citizen or resident alien is subject to tax on worldwide income from all sources
Form 3520 is required for receipt of more than USD 100,000 in gifts or bequests from a nonresident alien individual or foreign estate

sources.title_en: Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements
supports: Form 8938 thresholds for a specified individual living in the United States: more than USD 50,000 on the last day of the year or more than USD 75,000 at any time (single / married filing separately); USD 100,000 / USD 150,000 for married filing jointly
Form 8938 thresholds for a specified individual living outside the United States: USD 200,000 / USD 300,000 single; USD 400,000 / USD 600,000 joint
Form 8938 penalty: up to USD 10,000, plus USD 10,000 for each 30 days of non-filing after notice, maximum USD 60,000
FBAR threshold: aggregate value of financial accounts exceeds USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year
FBAR civil penalty: for assessments before 1 August 2016, non-willful up to USD 10,000; willful up to the greater of USD 100,000 or 50 percent of account balances

sources.title_en: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
supports: A U.S. person with a financial interest in or signature authority over at least one foreign financial account must file FinCEN Form 114 where the aggregate value exceeded USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year
Due 15 April with an automatic extension to 15 October
Civil FBAR penalty maximums in Title 31 are adjusted annually for inflation
Records generally kept five years from the FBAR due date

sources.title_en: Gifts from foreign person (Form 3520, Part IV)
supports: Receipt of more than USD 100,000 in aggregate from a nonresident alien individual or foreign estate in a taxable year must be reported; each gift over USD 5,000 separately identified
For purported gifts from foreign corporations or partnerships the threshold is USD 20,573 for 2026
Penalties may apply under IRC section 6039F(c)

sources.issuer: FinCEN, via the electronic Code of Federal Regulations
sources.title_en: 31 CFR 1010.821 - Penalty adjustment and table (inflation-adjusted maximums)
supports: 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I), willful FBAR violation: statutory USD 100,000, adjusted maximum USD 165,353 for penalties assessed on or after 17 January 2025
31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(B)(i), non-willful FBAR violation: statutory USD 10,000, adjusted maximum USD 16,536
31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(1), general willful BSA violation: range USD 71,545 to USD 286,184
sources.retrieval_note: Table read on eCFR (title 31 current to 2026-11-05). These are maximums, not assessments; the willful penalty is also capped as a percentage of the balance by statute.
